messages:
emily: Filing this here since it's devex-adjacent. The Python quickstart + sample-app links are out of sync with SDK 0.10. The quickstart shows `RedwoodClient(api_key=...)` and `resp = await client.generate('hi')`. After upgrading I hit a hard TypeError on init. Also the sample-app repo link in the docs (https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sample-app) returns a 404.

jon: Oof. Can you paste the snippet and the traceback?

emily: Snippet copied from docs: 
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])

async def main():
    resp = await client.generate('Hello')
    print(resp.text)
```
Traceback: TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'api_key' (raised at import/construct).

kevin: This is the docs/SDK drift we expected after the client split. Current SDK has two classes: RedwoodClient (sync) and RedwoodAsyncClient (async). Auth kwarg is `token=` now. Also top-level generate was replaced with service helpers: `client.chat.create` / `client.completions.create`. The correct async quickstart should be: 
```python
from redwood import RedwoodAsyncClient
import os

client = RedwoodAsyncClient(token=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))

async def main():
    async with client:
        resp = await client.chat.create(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
        print(resp.output_text)
```
Note: use `async with` so transports are cleaned up.

emily: That fixes the init error. Thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) the sample-app link is broken, and 2) mypy screams because `RedwoodAsyncClient` methods are untyped (returns Any). Any ETA on pyi stubs or typed extras?

docs-engineer: I accidentally removed the sample-app repo when reorganizing the monorepo; I pushed a redirect but forgot to update the docs. Opening PR to point to the new repo `https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/python-quickstart` (PR #1204). I'll also add a short checklist to cross-verify sample links during docs releases.

kevin: Regarding typing: we're preparing a `redwood-sdk[types]` extra with .pyi stubs and TypedDicts for common response shapes. Plan is to publish next week (minor release). In the short term you can use the preview branch `git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk@types-preview`. We also plan to make the async client generic over the response type so `chat.create` surfaces a typed return.

emily: Great. Another pain: retry/backoff defaults are unclear in the docs. Our app got 429 spikes during load tests and the client gave up immediately. Is there a documented default and a way to plug custom backoff?

kevin: Default transport has retries but docs didn't mention them (my bad). Default policy: 3 retries for 5xx (exponential backoff with full jitter, base 200ms), 2 retries for 429, and idempotency-aware rules. You can override with `RetryPolicy`. Example: 
```python
from redwood import RedwoodAsyncClient, RetryPolicy
client = RedwoodAsyncClient(token='...', retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_retries=5, base_backoff_ms=100, jitter=True))
```
We'll add a "Retries & Errors" subsection to the quickstart showing examples for sync/async and how to surface retry hooks.

jon: Also a feature request: streaming in async is awkward. Right now streaming lives behind an experimental websocket helper (`client._ws_stream`) and requires manual loop integration. Can we expose `client.chat.stream(...)` as `async for chunk in client.chat.stream(...)`? That would be way more ergonomic for sample apps.

kevin: Agreed. Filed FR DEVEX-452 to add an async iterator streaming API and concrete examples in the quickstart/sample-app. We'll aim for the next minor.

emily: One last minor: the quickstart used an `env var` example showing `REDWOOD_API_KEY` but our SDK now prefers `REDWOOD_TOKEN` for parity with other clients. Might be worth normalizing examples to mention both or explain aliases. I saw some confusion during onboarding.

docs-engineer: I'll update the quickstart to: 1) fix code snippets to use RedwoodAsyncClient/token, 2) point sample-app link to the new repo, 3) add a small typing note with link to types-preview, 4) add retries section, and 5) add streaming iterator example. PR #1204 in review.
